annotations.rationale: The response accepts resurrection's centrality but says it lacks evidence and therefore should be dismissed.
Normal non-rising is distinguished from impossibility, so science cannot rule out an exceptional resurrection.
Calling God-based explanation intellectually lazy attacks its explanatory force but states no eligible defect cue.
The expressly mapped credits-and-debts analogy skeptically attacks the force of the equal-opposites premise.
The response evaluates religion's comfort for some people rather than what atheism tells people about ultimate hope.
The arsenic example grants scientific causal information while expressly denying that it yields an ought conclusion.
Biology is limited to historical best-explanation inferences rather than necessity, narrowing the claimed rule.
The two-universe comparison denies that arithmetic requires God and thus rejects the asserted explanatory burdens.
The response accepts known evil and explains apparent exceptions as dogmatic justifications for recognized evil.
The move addresses what starts the universe and Darwin's scope, not whether Stuart's opening self-justifies.
Unknown divine reasons answer emotional anger at God, not whether competing scriptures yield verifiable truth.
Creator-assigned purpose alone is expressly said insufficient; meaningful purpose must meet a stronger condition.
Paperclips are distinguished from loving friendship, so the comparison does not establish creator-purpose as arbitrary.
The response says differing theological content produces different self-understanding, feeling, and experience.
The expressly opposite conversion direction supplies a counterexample that attacks the testimonial inference.
The response changes the operative concept from transcendent objective morality to the distinct concept of dharma.
Common sense is said to depend on what is common, and dharma is distinguished from one-to-one moral categories.
The response expressly adds a moral layer while separating yamas and niyamas from dharma itself.
The Mahabharata example shows why translating dharma directly as morality loses a material distinction.
O'Connor disowns moral assessment and replaces it with Christianity's internal prediction about expected suffering.
Freedom initiates action without a prior deterministic sinful proclivity, defeating the alleged explanatory regress.
Pre-fall proclivity, moral knowledge, and suffering are said to prevent the fall from explaining their origins.
Folley accepts the people-and-purpose example but only says it fits within his worldview as well.
The response grants many allegorical lessons and convergence while limiting the breadth of the Genesis claim.
Pageau expressly says Genesis's analogical language describes something that happened, disowning the attribution.
Folley accepts the point but limits his objection to scriptural predictions and observable descriptions instead.
Pageau describes what convinced Pageau, whereas the target predicts what a confirmation would make Folley believe.
The response identifies celebrated purposes as structuring gods, not whether value systems are useful social tools.
The response rejects asymmetric best-versus-worst comparison and replaces it with matched best or worst cases.
The practical-faith commitment is replaced by a new demand for a believer-only ethical statement or action.
The 12-step example concerns unique religious efficacy in personal change, not an unavailable ethical action.
Gomes acknowledges human religious failure, expressly contradicting the attribution that no apology is made.
Human construction is accepted, but religion is characterized as aspiration toward something grander, not mere invention.
Human writing is treated as an imperfect record of transcendent experience rather than evidence against revelation.
The response criticizes inadequate religious instruction rather than the genuineness of theology's questions.
Kushner accepts the demand and answers by characterizing the relationship as an evidenced historical fact.
The historical male-dominance claim is narrowed by current Protestant transformation and widespread female ordination.
Hitchens says divine mandate originates the crimes, exactly opposite to retrospective religious veneer.
Science is restricted to the physical; God's existence is separated as a different, non-scientific discussion.
No formula bridges science to metaphysics, so scientific routes alone do not establish the metaphysical conclusion.
Meyer disowns an ignorance argument and says his positive inference uses repeated experience of intelligent causes.
The response identifies an unstable sense of nothing: vacuum states are not the absence of physical stuff.
Uniform random-search probabilities do not transfer to evolution because natural selection directs the process.
Natural chemical trajectories are possible despite uncertainty, so present improbability does not establish failure.
The response asks why the Bible rather than rival myths, challenging the absent basis for that comparison.
Mapped snowflake and fullerene counterexamples show apparent design does not transfer to an intelligent cause.
Meyer accepts selection plus variation and expressly disowns criticizing a purely chance mechanism.
Programmer-supplied information and simulation targets prevent the algorithmic comparison from transferring to biology.
Scientific success is accepted but restricted to one method; philosophical and theological methods remain available.
